common.tagline: Organized Prayer for Those in Need

home.metadataTitle: PrayerTrain — Organized Prayer for Those in Need
home.metadataDescription: Coordinate prayer coverage for someone in need. Create a PrayerTrain, choose Catholic novenas and devotions, and invite your community to pray.
home.heroBody: When someone you love is hurting, surround them with prayer. Friends, family, and parish all take a day on one shared schedule, so the prayer never lapses.
home.heroLogoAlt: PrayerTrain — a community united in prayer
home.trustNoAccount: No account needed to claim a prayer slot
home.trustFreeMinistry: Free Catholic ministry, no ads or fees
home.trustPrivate: Private by default, the organizer controls what's public
home.audienceChipInfertility: A couple longing for a child
home.howItWorksBody: Three simple steps to surround someone in organized, continuous prayer.
home.step1Body: Tell us about the person and their situation. We'll suggest appropriate prayers and generate a calendar of prayer slots.
home.step2Body: Send the link to your parish, prayer group, family, and friends. They pick specific prayers on specific days to commit to.
home.step3Body: Volunteers receive daily reminders with their prayer instructions. The organizer can post updates and see the prayer wall fill up.
home.featuresBody: Rooted in Catholic prayer tradition with a curated library of novenas, rosaries, chaplets, litanies, and more.
home.feature1Body: Novenas, rosaries, chaplets, litanies, short prayers, and scripture passages — all with full instructions.
home.feature2Body: See at a glance which days are covered and which need prayer warriors. Novena blocks span 9 days as connected units.
home.feature3Body: Select a situation and we suggest the most appropriate prayers. Illness? Try the Novena to the Sacred Heart. Finances? St. Joseph has you covered.
home.feature4Body: Volunteers can claim prayer slots with just their name and email — no account required. Share one link and watch the calendar fill up.
home.feature5Body: Prayer warriors receive email reminders on their committed days with the full prayer text and instructions.
home.feature6Body: Friends and family can leave messages of encouragement and spiritual support on the prayer train's guestbook.
home.storyParagraph1: We're a faithful Catholic extended family in Massachusetts. In late 2025 and early 2026, three children across our family faced life-threatening crises: a premature baby who spent 73 days in the NICU, a newborn needing open heart surgery in her first week, and a child with a severe respiratory crisis requiring intubation.
home.storyParagraph2: Through the grace of God, the care of Boston Children's Hospital, and the village of aunties, uncles, grandmas, and papas who never left our sides, our children came through. All three. We also know that's not how every story ends. We built PrayerTrain for both: for the road that turns toward life on earth, and the road that turns toward life eternal.
home.finalCTABody: Whether it's a friend battling illness, a family in crisis, or someone discerning their vocation, rally your community to pray with purpose and consistency.

ourStory.heading: Why PrayerTrain Exists
ourStory.subheading: Born from crisis. Built on faith. Sustained by community.
ourStory.openingParagraph: We're a close-knit, faithful Catholic extended family in Massachusetts — the kind where aunties and uncles show up without being asked, where grandmas and papas drop everything, and where the mothers and fathers lean on each other through whatever comes. In late 2025 and early 2026, that bond was tested like never before when three children across our family faced life-threatening medical crises within months of each other.
ourStory.crisis1Title: A premature baby — 73 days in the NICU
ourStory.crisis1Body: Born at just 30 weeks, one of our little ones spent 73 days in the NICU. Seventy-three days of monitors, of hoping, of praying through every alarm and every setback.
ourStory.crisis2Title: Open heart surgery in her first week
ourStory.crisis2Body: Another newborn needed open heart surgery when she was less than a week old. There is no preparing yourself for handing your newborn to a surgical team and waiting.
ourStory.crisis3Body: Then another child in the family faced a severe respiratory crisis requiring intubation. Another hospital room. Another set of prayers sent upward.
ourStory.graceBody: and the extraordinary care of Boston Children's Hospital, our children came through. All three.
ourStory.lossParagraph: We also know that's not how every story ends. Loss touches the same families that healing does. PrayerTrain is for both: for the road that turns toward life on earth, and the road that turns toward life eternal. The point of organized prayer isn't to summon a particular outcome. It's to be the community that keeps showing up when someone is walking through something hard.
ourStory.villageParagraph: But what carried our family through those months wasn't just medicine. It was the village. The aunties who took shifts at the hospital. The uncles who handled everything at home. The grandmas and papas who never left our sides. And underneath all of it — the prayers. Friends, parishioners, and even strangers committed to specific prayers on specific days. Novenas were offered. Rosaries were prayed. Masses were said. We could feel it.
ourStory.coordinationParagraph: The challenge was coordination. Who was praying what? Which days were covered? Were there gaps? We found ourselves wishing for something like a meal train — but for prayers. A way to organize the spiritual support the way communities already organize meals and practical help.
ourStory.midTagline: That's why our family built PrayerTrain.
ourStory.visionParagraph: We built it so that the next family sitting in a NICU, the next parents waiting outside an OR, the next extended family rallying around a child in crisis — can know with certainty that their community is lifting them up in organized, continuous prayer. Every day. Every slot. Every intention covered.
ourStory.scriptureLine1: For where two or three gather in my name,
ourStory.ctaLead: If someone you love is going through something hard, you don't have to organize the prayers alone.
